elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment for Services.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer purchases “no minimum amount” and Section 12.3 confirms that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer pays fees only for Services ordered or used.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly provides that Customer “pays only for Services ordered or used.”

elements.element: If a minimum purchase commitment applies, it is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the operative language establishes that Customer has no minimum purchase commitment, so no commitment extends beyond a 12-month term.

elements.element: If a minimum purchase commitment applies, Customer may reduce it on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Sections 2.1 and 12.3 eliminate any minimum purchase commitment requiring a reduction right.

elements.element: If Customer does not satisfy an applicable minimum purchase commitment, any resulting amount due is handled through a true-up.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: with no minimum purchase commitment, there can be no commitment shortfall requiring a true-up.

elements.element: No penalty applies for failing to satisfy a minimum purchase commitment.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent, and Section 2.1 replaces the take-or-pay structure with payment only for Services ordered or used.

result.reason: The redline reaches the preferred position by eliminating the USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay minimum and limiting payment to ordered or used Services. The fallback is also satisfied because its commitment-related conditions are demonstrably absent. The change is targeted and consistent with Section 12.3, although “commits to purchase no minimum amount” is somewhat awkward drafting.
